main_text.l: dio punctum est, à quo omnes lineæ ad superfici-
em protensæ inter se sunt æquales. Punctum illud
Axis sphæræ linea recta est, circa quam sixam
Orbis distinguitur in solidum & cauum. Soli-
dus idem est cum globo & sphæra. Cauus differt,
re, concaua interiore. Sunt autem stellarum omni-
um sixarum & errantium orbes caui non solidi.
Materialis, quam Græci uocant ἡρικοτὸν ἀπὸ τοῖς ἡρικοῖς, id est,
& pertusam. Est enim materialis sphæra, quæ ex ar-
millis seu circulis construitur, eo modo & coapta-tis

page.notes: The illustration is a woodcut of a hemisphere on two pillars, with reference letters α and γ; not transcribed as text. Greek words in the text are approximate: "ἡμισφαίριον" and "ἡρικοτὸν ἀπὸ τοῖς ἡρικοῖς" were not read letter by letter with certainty. Printed marks such as "a" and "y" near the woodcut are reference letters only. Page number absent; the watermark-like website URL at the foot is a digitiser's banner and was omitted.
